items.title: CustomRequest
items.text: CustomRequest is an effective routing plugin for MODX Revolution to map pretty but not found URLs to a MODX resource and to set the request parameters by separating the URI path at the URI separators or by a regular expression.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• MODX Revolution 2.6+
  • PHP 7.2+

items.title: Features
items.text: • Use pretty URLs everywhere in the MODX Revolution frontend.

items.title: License
items.text: The project is licensed under the GPLv2 license.

items.title: Translations
items.text: Translations of the package can be made for the Default Lexicon and the System Setting Lexicon.

items.title: Calendar
items.text:
With the Date configuration you can use a calendar snippet on the resource Date with the URI calendar/date/. The snippet on that resource uses the request parameters year, month, day, title to identify the event. An example URI triggering this configuration: /calendar/date/2015/09/01/eventname.html

The Calendar configuration sends the request parameters year, month, day to another snippet on the resource Calendar with the URI calendar/. Example triggering URI: /calendar/2015/09/01/ 1

Name Alias Path Resource URI Parameter Regular Expression Date calendar/date/ Date ["year", "month", "day", "title"] Calendar calendar/ Calendar ["year", "month", "day"]

items.title: Gallery
items.text:
With the Gallery configuration you can use the Gallery snippet on the selected resource Gallery Folder. The Gallery snippet on that resource uses the request parameters galAlbum, galItem to identify the gallery and the image. An example URI triggering this configuration: /gallery/01/02/

Name Alias Path Resource URI Parameter Regular Expression Gallery Gallery Folder ["galAlbum", "galItem"]

items.title: Different URI
items.text:
With the Different URI configuration you can call the resource Test with a completely different URI using the request parameters parameter1, parameter2. 2

Name Alias Path Resource URI Parameter Regular Expression Different URI complete/different/uri/ Test ["parameter1", "parameter2"]

items.title: Regular Expression
items.text:
You can even use regular expressions5 to set the request parameters. 3

Name Alias Path Resource URI Parameter Regular Expression Expression Expression ["string", "numeric"] #(.*?)-(\d+)#

items.title: Pagination
items.text:
The Alias Path field can be filled with a valid regular expression5 (the grid value is shown with blue text then4) and the Resource field can stay empty. That way you can use one pagination configuration for all pagination calls on the site. The first subpattern (page/) of the expression is stripped from the found pattern and the remaining string is used to identify the resource the user is forwarded to.

Name Alias Path Resource URI Parameter Regular Expression Pagination #.*?(page/)# ["page"] #(\d+)#

items.text:
CustomRequest uses the following system settings in the namespace customrequest:

Key Description Default customrequest.debug Log debug information in the MODX error log No

  1. If you are using two or more nested aliases in your configurations, the deeper alias has to be defined before the narrower alias. You can drag and drop the configurations in the grid of the custom manager page. ↩

  2. The Alias Path does not have to match the alias of the Resource. ↩

  3. This rule does not make much sense. If you have a real world example, please open an issue in the GitHub repository. ↩

  4. The regular expression5 has to be valid and it has to contain delimiters. ↩

  5. To build and check regular expressions you can use e.g. the regex101 website. ↩↩↩

items.title: Install from MODX Extras
items.text: Search for CustomRequest in the Package Manager of your MODX installation and install it in there.

items.title: Manual installation
items.text:
If you can't access the MODX Extras Repository in your MODX installation, you can manually install CustomRequest.

  • Download the transport package from MODX Extras (or one of the pre built transport packages in _packages)
  • Upload the zip file to your MODX installation's core/packages folder or upload it manually in the MODX Package Manager.
  • In the MODX Manager, navigate to the Package Manager page, and select 'Search locally for packages' from the dropdown button.
  • CustomRequest should now show up in the list of available packages. Click the corresponding 'Install' button and follow the instructions to complete the installation.

items.title: Build it from source
items.text: To build and install the package from source you could use Git Package Management. The GitHub repository of CustomRequest contains a config.json to build that package locally. Use this option, if you want to debug CustomRequest and/or contribute bugfixes and enhancements.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
CustomRequest works as a routing plugin. It maps not found URLs to a MODX resource and sets additional request parameters by separating the URI path at the URI separators or by a regular expression.

By default, the first characters of the not found URI are compared with the alias path of each configuration. If they match, this configuration is used. The alias path is stripped from the not found URI and the remaining string is used to set the request parameters.

Alternatively, the alias path of a configuration can contain a valid regular expression and the not found URI is matched with that expression. If it matches, this configuration is used. The first subpattern of the expression is stripped from the found pattern and the remaining string is used to identify the resource the user is forwarded to. Finally, the found pattern is removed from the not found URI and the remaining string is used to set the request parameters.

In multilingual installations, e.g. with Babel, a leading culture key of the current context (like de/) is removed from the not found URI before it is compared.

items.title: Request parameters
items.text:
The remaining string is divided at the URI separators / (or by the regular expression of the configuration) and the parts are assigned to the keys of the URI Parameter field in their order. Parts without a key are assigned to p1, p2 and so on, according to their position, e.g. the third part is assigned to p3. A .html in the remaining string is removed before.

The parameters are set in $_GET and $_REQUEST, so a snippet on the resource can use them like normal request parameters. If the regular expression of a configuration does not match the remaining string, the request is not forwarded.

items.title: Custom Manager Page
items.text:
You can configure CustomRequest in a custom manager page in the extras menu. The CustomRequest configurations are created on that page.

The configurations are executed in the order of the grid on this page. If there are two configurations starting with the same alias path, the first configuration is used. You can change the order of the configurations by drag and drop.

The following settings can be set in each configuration:

Key Description Name A name to identify this configuration. Alias Path

By default, the first characters of a not found URI are compared with this string. If they match, this configuration is used. If the alias path field is not set, the alias path of the selected resource in this form is used (the grid value is shown with green text then). The alias path is stripped from the not found URI and the remaining string is used to set the request parameters.

Alternatively, this field can contain a valid regular expression1 (the grid value is shown with blue text then). The regular expression has to contain delimiters. The not found URI is matched with that expression. If it matches, this configuration is used. The first subpattern of the expression is stripped from the found pattern and the remaining string is used to identify the resource the user is forwarded to. Finally, the found pattern is removed from the not found URI and the remaining string is used to set the request parameters.

If no resource is selected, the alias path has to be a regular expression.

Resource A not found URI is forwarded to this resource, if the current configuration is used and if the alias path does not contain a regular expression. URI Parameter A JSON array of request parameter keys, e.g. ["year", "month"]. The parts of the not found URI after the alias path are assigned to these keys in their order. If the Regular Expression field is not set, the URI is divided at the URI separators /. Regular Expression This optional regular expression1 is used to divide the remaining string of the not found URI. The regular expression has to contain delimiters. The subpatterns are assigned to the request parameters in the order of occurrence.

  1. To build and check regular expressions you can use e.g. the regex101 website. Please use the code generator, since this generator creates the regular expression with delimiters. ↩↩
